title: Memory-Efficient Attention Mechanisms for Transformer Training
problem: Attention mechanisms in transformers are memory bandwidth bottlenecks during training, consuming significant intermediate tensor storage. This memory consumption limits model scalability and training throughput.
motivation: Reducing memory bandwidth bottlenecks directly improves transformer training speed, enables larger model scalability, and increases hardware utilization efficiency.
method: The work proposes a fused attention kernel that combines multiple attention computation stages into a single kernel invocation. By eliminating intermediate tensor materialization and optimizing memory access patterns, the approach reduces bandwidth requirements while preserving numerical accuracy through careful algorithm design.
key_novelty: Fusing attention operations into a single kernel to eliminate intermediate memory materialization and directly optimize memory bandwidth utilization.
contributions: Fused attention kernel achieving 60% memory bandwidth reduction
Maintains numerical accuracy compared to standard implementations
Improved transformer training efficiency and scalability
Generalizable methodology for various transformer architectures
